body:
# Energy wire, Nov 25 (one-line wire items, originals not read)

| Object | Read | State |
|---|---|---|
| Hodeidah, 12:48Z | 'Saudi forces reportedly target Hodeidah port, according to Al Mayadeen' | **CLAIM ONLY** (Houthi-aligned outlet). New or a late relay of the early-Wednesday strike (card 20261124-006): not established |
| Saree, 11:52Z feed, 12:12Z page | Jeddah and Saudi Red Sea ports a target **if** Hodeidah is bombed | if genuinely new, the order is warning, then a reported strike about an hour later: **a second round on the same day**. Card 008 called it possibly a late relay; still open |
| Strike on a Saudi Red Sea port | none found | not found by my search |
| Kazakhstan | oil and condensate 1.74 mb/d on Nov 24, 17% under its November average; unstable loadings at the CPC Black Sea terminal forced curbs ('source reports') | unnamed sources; CPC and Kazakh ministry not read. Arithmetic: average about 2.10, so about 0.36 mb/d under it on one day |
| Kazakhstan and OPEC+ | dissatisfied with the capacity assessment, seeks a higher quota | sources; not opened |
| Putin, 13:21Z | Russia will answer Ukrainian refinery attacks; wants talks on energy infrastructure; **says Trump asked Ukraine to halt strikes on refineries** | Putin's claim; no US or Ukrainian confirmation found |
| Russia fuel bans | Novak: aviation-fuel export ban (to Nov 30) proposed for extension; gasoline ban beyond January considered in December | wire line, not opened |

- **So what:** BRENT has two supply-side facts pulling against a falling price (Brent vendor about 89.3): a Black Sea loading loss and a Red Sea threat whose condition is met. OSPREY owns the refinery-strike talks claim.
